title: Wren and the Winter
premise: Felix Underhill, a pest controller in the dying village of Wren's Hollow, is called to investigate noises in the church — noises that turn out to be made by something with human fingerprints, pressing through the walls from the other side of the world. When the melted bell of 1911 rings again, Felix learns the village founders bound a hungry presence beneath the chapel with a ritual of memory: each generation, one keeper must feed it their most cherished recollections until nothing of them remains. The last keeper, her grandmother, died with the ritual unfinished, and now the thing is awake, wearing the faces and fingerprints of everyone the village has forgotten. To save the village, Felix must complete the ritual — but the price is every memory she holds of the person she loves, and the presence has learned that love is the richest food of all. In the end, Felix feeds it her memories one by one until only love itself remains, a feeling with no object, and that nameless devotion proves the one thing the presence cannot digest; she seals it back beneath the church, whole but hollow, as the villagers — who no longer remember her — lay flowers on a stranger's grave.
about_author: Zephyrine Fairweather is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the belongings of the dead in rural England. Their fiction has appeared in several small-press horror anthologies, and they live near a church whose bell has not rung since 1911.

chapters.title: The Fingerprint in the Wall
chapters.summary: Felix Underhill, pest controller, is called to Wren's Hollow chapel to deal with scratching in the walls. She finds no droppings, no nests — only a perfect human fingerprint pressed into the plaster from the inside. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: professional skepticism curdling into quiet dread.

chapters.title: Village of the Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Felix canvasses villagers for pest history and notices everyone speaks of the past in odd, gapped sentences — names missing mid-story, faces they can't place. An old woman, Mrs. Tallow, grips Felix's wrist and says, 'You have her hands.' POV: Felix. Emotional beat: uncanny loneliness; the village is forgetting something on purpose.

chapters.title: The Bell That Was Not There
chapters.summary: At 3:11 a.m., the chapel bell rings — though parish records show it was melted for scrap in 1911. Felix, sleepless, watches villagers step out of their cottages and walk toward the church as if summoned, faces slack. She follows. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the moment explanation dies and horror begins.

chapters.title: Under the Floor
chapters.summary: In the crypt, Felix finds a hatch sealed with iron and wax, and scratched into its underside — readable only from below — hundreds of names. The last is her grandmother's. The scratching from chapter one resumes, directly beneath her feet, patient as breathing. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: personal stakes revealed; this has been waiting for her.

chapters.title: What Mrs. Tallow Gave Up
chapters.summary: Mrs. Tallow tells Felix the founders' covenant: a keeper feeds the thing below their memories, one cherished recollection per year, to keep it asleep. She shows Felix the gap in her own life — she had a husband once, she thinks, and cannot even miss him. POV: Felix, with Tallow's recounted memories. Emotional beat: grief for losses that leave no scar.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix searches her grandmother's abandoned cottage and finds the keeper's ledger: decades of entries describing memories in loving detail, then the final entry, unfinished — a ritual half-performed, the binding left open for five years. The last line names Felix by name. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: inheritance as sentence; duty she never agreed to.

chapters.title: It Wears the Forgotten
chapters.summary: The presence begins manifesting as the people the village has forgotten: a postman no one can name, children in the lanes whom no parent claims. Felix realizes it is built from everything the keepers fed it — memory given flesh, and hungry for more. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: horror of being surrounded by other people's discarded love.

chapters.title: Eden
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Felix and Eden, the person she loves, five years ago in this same village, before Felix left and before her grandmother's death. Their happiness on the page makes what's coming unbearable. POV: Eden, in flashback. Emotional beat: warmth deliberately planted to be harvested.

chapters.title: The First Payment
chapters.summary: The thing breaches the crypt and takes a memory from Felix without consent — her mother's face. She wakes knowing she had a mother but unable to picture her. Eden arrives in the village, worried after Felix's calls, and Felix cannot explain why she is crying. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: violation; the ritual has already begun, whether she consents or not.

chapters.title: The Founders' Bargain
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Felix reads the founders' original pact: they summoned the presence deliberately, to devour the village's grief after a plague, and bound it only when it refused to stop eating. Power, they learned, is a mouth that never closes. POV: Felix, reading documents. Emotional beat: the horror is human-made; the village chose this.

chapters.title: Eden Remembers Enough for Two
chapters.summary: Eden, unaffected by the covenant, begins noticing the gaps — and notices Felix is disappearing from photographs, from shared stories. She confronts Felix, who lies badly. The presence watches their argument from an upstairs window, wearing Felix's own face. POV: Eden. Emotional beat: love against duty's first open collision.

chapters.title: A Feast of Small Things
chapters.summary: The presence, impatient, begins feeding indiscriminately: villagers lose whole decades overnight. The village descends into gentle, smiling ruin — people who cannot remember why they are sad, or that they are. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the corruption of power; the covenant protects the village by emptying it.

chapters.title: The Second Payment
chapters.summary: To stop the indiscriminate feeding, Felix performs the ritual voluntarily for the first time, choosing her own memory: the day her grandmother taught her to ring the bell. The presence is sated — briefly — and speaks to her for the first time, in her grandmother's voice. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the terrible relief of complicity.

chapters.title: What the Presence Wants
chapters.summary: Through her grandmother's stolen voice, the presence bargains: finish the ritual, and it will return everything it took — every villager's memories, her mother's face. Felix wants to believe it. Eden warns her that a thing made of memory cannot be trusted to give any back. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: temptation; the devil's arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Keeper
chapters.summary: Felix deciphers her grandmother's final, unfinished entry and learns the truth: her grandmother didn't die of illness — she gave the presence everything, including the memory of the ritual itself, and the binding broke because no one alive remembered how to close it. The instructions are in the memories it ate. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the trap closes; the cure is inside the disease.

chapters.title: Descent with a Candle
chapters.summary: Felix opens the hatch and goes down into the dark beneath the crypt, into a space lined with pressed fingerprints, where the eaten memories hang like frost. She must walk into the thing itself to retrieve her grandmother's final memory. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: courage as a choice made while terrified.

chapters.title: The Archive of the Eaten
chapters.summary: Inside, Felix experiences the villagers' surrendered memories as her own — weddings, funerals, first snows — and nearly loses herself among them, forgetting which life is hers. Eden's voice, calling down the hatch, is her thread back. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: memory as identity; love as an anchor.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Last Memory
chapters.summary: Felix finds the final memory: her grandmother, dying, chose to leave the binding open — because closing it forever would require a keeper to surrender not just memories but the capacity to love, and she refused to sentence Felix to that. She left the door open hoping Felix would find another way. POV: Felix, inside the memory. Emotional beat: inherited love as both burden and absolution.

chapters.title: The Presence Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: The presence drops its masks and offers Felix the true bargain: give it Eden — not her memories of Eden, but Eden herself, body and all — and it will sleep for a thousand years, needing nothing else. It has learned that one great love outweighs ten thousand small memories. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the climax of love against duty; the cruelest possible choice.

chapters.title: The Ritual Completed
chapters.summary: Felix refuses — and instead feeds it everything, all at once: every memory she owns, a lifetime in a single swallow, hoping to choke it. The presence gorges, reels, and in its gluttony Felix speaks the closing words from her grandmother's memory. The bell rings one last time and falls silent. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy; giving everything to keep the one thing that matters.

chapters.title: The Hollow Woman
chapters.summary: Felix wakes in the snow above the sealed crypt with no memories at all — except one feeling that would not go down: love, vast and objectless. Eden finds her and does not know her; the village does not know her; she does not know herself. But when Eden passes, something in her chest turns toward him like a compass. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: devastating cost; the ghost of love outliving its content.

chapters.title: Flowers for a Stranger
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Eden keeps returning to the village without knowing why, and keeps bringing flowers to a grave with no name. Felix, relearning the world from scratch, keeps finding herself drawn to the churchyard at dusk. Two strangers keep almost meeting. The bell does not ring. POV: alternating Felix and Eden. Emotional beat: resolution without restoration — memory is gone, but love, the thing beneath memory, begins again.
